MISSION OF THE 
MONTREAL 


YMCA 


“The Montreal YMCA is a partnership of 
volunteers and staff committed to the 
fulfillment of people in spirit, mind and 
body and to the development of 
self-reliance in the individual and the 
community. 


Through its actions, programs and 
services, the Montreal YMCA reflects the 
needs and aspirations of communities 
and works with individuals, local 
communities and communities in 
developing countries in achieving social 
justice and control of their environments.” 


: MESSAGE FROM THE CHAIR 
: Bringing OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS 
Quality to Life AND THE PRESIDENT & CHIEF 
EXECUTIVE OFFICER 


YMCA 


J 


We build strong kids, strong families, strong communities. This one sentence sums up 
the driving force behind the larger North American YMCA family for the past few years. 


Yet this is not a new direction for the Montreal YMCA. Even the most cursory 
glance at the annual report will show you that the Montreal YMCA has always 
focused on youth of all ages and the well-being of their families. The YMCA also 
works hard to turn every community into a warm and welcoming place where 
everyone feels at home. 


When we refer to the Montreal YMCA, we mean the 1,200 employees and 1,700 
volunteers who are part of the daily life in YMCA centres. They put all their energy 
into the YMCA so that everyone can live a happier and more dynamic life. We want 
them to know that when we renovate, restructure or set up new programs, our goal is 
to also make their lives easier and enable them to work in a more pleasant 
environment. 


This annual report naturally contains numbers and results, but it also speaks of more 
intangible concepts like courage and commitment. In our tour of the various centres, 
we make way for the men and women who truly breathe life into the YMCA. This is 
our way of expressing gratitude for what they do. 


In closing, we also wish to thank the members of the Board of Directors and of the 
Montreal YMCA Foundation for their generosity and support. 


oa Mba 


Louise Jolicoeur Michael Weil 
Chair of the Board of Directors President & Chief Executive Officer 


KIDS 


THE TEDDY 
BEAR MAN 


Pierre Méthot is a 
volunteer at the 
Guy-Favreau YMCA. 
For the past ten 
years, he has tracked 4 
down teddy bears for [i & 
children who are 6 
victims of family 
violence or who live ~ 
in shelters. In ten : ay 
years, he has collected 18,000 stuffed toys 
to brighten up children’s lives. 


This campaign is only one of four that 
Pierre organizes every year to help individuals 
and families in difficulty. He also organizes 
social and cultural outings, which enable 
more than 300 people to spend a day in the 
country, visit a museum or another city. 
Once again this year, members and 
participants at the Guy-Favreau YMCA have 
generously supported Pierre’s efforts.

STRONG 


KANAWANA - THE 
CAMP WHERE 
EVERYONE IS 
WELCOME 


Fifteen hundred 
campers came from the 
Montreal area last 
summer, but also from | 
Africa, Asia, Europe and 
South America. Children 
from all backgrounds 
enjoyed an incredible 
two-week camping 
experience. Fifty-two 
of them benefited from 
the financial-assistance program. 


Camp facilities were also used to train counsellors, 
and hold anti-violence programs for teenage girls 
and other groups. 


This year, the number of camp volunteers from all 
YMCA centres increased significantly. Who says 
that volunteerism is plummeting? 


AN ALTERNATIVE TO 
SCHOOL SUSPENSIONS 


Concerned about the increased number of teens at 
the Du Parc YMCA during school hours, youth 
workers decided to find out more about the 
school-suspension problem. When left on 

their own, youth who were temporarily 

suspended from school were more 
likely to drop out or become 
juvenile delinquents. 


They therefore developed an 
assistance program in cooperation 
with school boards and the 
National Crime Prevention 
Centre. Suspended youth are 
directed to the YMCA for periods of 
3 to 5 days during which youth 
workers help them define their 
expectations regarding school, acquire 
self-assurance and catch up on school work. 


so ell — 


NDG: A YOUTH-ORIENTED 
COMMUNITY 


Every year, hundreds of youth of all ages spend 
time at the Notre-Dame-de-Grace YMCA. Parents 
feel confident entrusting their toddlers here. 
Youth are attracted by the gym, the 
opportunity to be among their 
peers, to participate in friendly 
basketball tournaments, etc.... 


Staff members and numerous 
volunteers (of which there are more 
than one hundred!) are on hand to 
provide supervision. They build 
relationships of trust with youth 

during leisure activities, which 
creates a foundation for them to help 
youth on other levels such as motivation, 

tutoring and conflict-resolution. This 
year, YMCA activities in this field served as a 
model for several schools. 


02, OXYGEN FOR CREATIVITY 


02 was launched this year by a number of 
community organizations, including the 
Pointe-Saint-Charles YMCA, as well as several 
local volunteer artists. The program helps 
inner-city children explore various forms of 
artistic expression. 


Using video, graphic arts, costume design, 
architecture, photography and puppet 
theatre, sixteen children from the YMCA 
realized for the first time in their lives that 
they too have talent. They also discovered 
that learning can be both enjoyable and 
rewarding. 


Week after week, children were encouraged 
by volunteer painters, filmmakers, writers, 
photographers, graphic designers, 
carpenters and sculptors who introduced 
them to their art. As a result, the 
children organized an exhibition at the 
Saidye Bronfman Centre for the Arts. You 
should have seen the pride on those 
shining faces!

BETWEEN SCHOOL AND HOME 


School finishes early and parents work late. 
The options for that “between time” are 
limited: daycare service or an after-school 
program (often too costly), television or the 
street. Since February 1999, youth at the 
Hochelaga-Maisonneuve YMCA have another 
alternative. Staff and volunteers spend 
several hours with youth to help them with

TOWARD FAMILY

invited children from underprivileged and 
isolated families in the community to join 


its day camp at a reduced price. 


This first step enabled community workers 
in the Downtown YMCA to make families 
aware of its early-childhood development 
programs and progressively gain their trust. 
It also gave community workers an 
opportunity to better define and understand

WE BUILD 
STRONG 


COMMUNITIES 


THE DOWNTOWN YMCA TAKES 
TO THE STREETS 


The upcoming renovation of the Downtown YMCA 
did not prevent staff and volunteers from taking 
to the streets. 


The City of Montreal and Destination Centre-ville 
decided to continue funding the Downtown YMCA's 
pilot Dialogue Project after it was so successful 
last year. The purpose of the project is to 
establish harmonious relationships among 
downtown residents, merchants and the homeless. 


With a goal of improving downtown life, YMCA 
staff, volunteers, members, participants and 
neighbours participated in the 3rd Cleanup Rally 
to mark Earth Day. 


WESTMOUNT YMCA 
HOSTS FIRST Y SHOW 


To showcase its programs and raise funds for 
community activities, the Westmount YMCA 
organized a first-time event starring YMCA staff, 
volunteers and other participants. The show 
featured singers, Highland dancers, jazz and belly 
dancers, tai-chi enthusiasts, kick boxers, men in 
step and mothers exercising with their babies in 
strollers. The colourful and dynamic program will 
only serve to further enhance the YMCA’s image in 
the community, which is already renowned for its 
members who are very attached to “their” Y. 


AME-ART FOR MILE-END 
ARTISTS 


Early in the summer of 1998, women in the 
Du Parc YMCA Family Program and several 
community workers decided to help out 
local artists who lack space, work in 
isolation and poverty, and who have 
limited entrepreneurial 
4 skills. 


Through a subsidy from the 
Anti-Poverty Fund, the 
YMCA was able to hire 
two community workers to 
help set up a co-op for the 
artists. 


The AME-ART co-op now 
groups together fifteen 
people who are truly 


determined to improve 


~ conditions for artists in 
the community by sharing work space, 
materials and services. As a result, there is 
greater solidarity emerging among the 
artists. The co-op 
has already organized 
its first exhibition 
and published a 
directory of member 
artists.

THE MONTREAL 


YMCA 


IN THE COMMUNICATIONS AGE 


Three years ago, the Montreal YMCA 
conducted an in-depth study of its 
communications with a goal of implementing 
a more strategic marketing and 
communications plan. 


The primary purpose of the plan was to 
generate and increase awareness of the 
many facets of our activities, while 
presenting a strong, professional and highly 
credible image to the public. We also 
sought to promote our programs to the 
right groups by better targeting our 
campaigns. 


The plan was a success. By harmonizing 
our advertising, information materials, and 
promotional activities, all centres benefited 
from our improved image as confirmed by 
the general increase in memberships. 


One noteworthy point is that the annual 
cost of our communications activities is no 
higher than it was before. Yet the results 
are far superior. 


«By harmonizing our advertising, 
information materials, and promotional 


activities, all centres benefited from our 
improved image as confirmed by the 
general increase in memberships.»

MONTREAL 


YMCA 


FOUNDATION 


: MESSAGE FROM THE 
: Bringing CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD 
Quality to Life OF DIRECTORS AND THE 
PRESIDENT OF THE MONTREAL 


YMCA 


eT YMCA FOUNDATION 


The role of the Foundation is to ensure long-term funding for the Montreal YMCA in 
order for our centres to play a front-line role in the community, and ensure access 
to our programs for all. 


The most striking accomplishment in this fiscal period is, without a doubt, the 
tremendous success of our campaign to revitalize the YMCA and its downtown facilities. 
Our goal was to raise $20 million, and we have reached $18 million to date! This is 
before even launching the final stage of the campaign that will be directed at the 
larger YMCA family and members of the community. 


Work will start this fall and be completed before the end of the Year 2000. As part 
of the project, the Drummond Tower will be demolished and the Norris Building will 
be renovated to house the new YMCA. During construction, the YMCA will continue 
to provide uninterrupted services and activities. 


However, this major project has not made us lose sight of our primary goal, which is 
to fund numerous community programs, provide support to participants in financial 
difficulty, and refurbish our various centres. Nevertheless, the visibility from the 
YMCA Revitalization Campaign is sure to benefit the entire 

Association. 


As we close the books on this fiscal period, we are proud of our accomplishments 
and ready for the next millennium. We wish to express our deepest gratitude to the 
Campaign President and Campaign Committee members for having taken this 
challenge to heart. We're on the home stretch! We also wish to thank some 100 
volunteers who will lend a hand for the final stage of the campaign. 


Furthermore, we wish to thank all of our donors. Their very generous donations 
only serve to confirm that the YMCA continues to play an important role in Montreal 
life.
